newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank says sees no sign of inflation pressure.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank says sees no sign of inflation pressure.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Wednesday it saw no sign of inflationary pressure in the German economy but that monetary policy will have to ensure prices remain stable over the long term.
"At the moment, inflationary impulses are not recognisable either from the demand side or from cost pressures," the German central bank said in its monthly report for June.
The report said inflation has remained low in part because of moderate wage increases and stable import prices despite foreign exchange market fluctuations.
The central bank said monetary policy must now ensure that inflation remains low.
"Monetary policy will have to make sure and safeguard this successful stability over the long-term," the report said.
